question.problem: Consider the plane curve $x{e}^{y}-1=xy.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(1,0).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x{e}^{y}-1 & =xy \\ x{e}^{y}-xy & =1\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=x{e}^{y}-xy$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=1.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(1,0)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(1,0)={f}_{y}(1,0)i-{f}_{x}(1,0)j
$$

 

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(1,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{y}-xy)i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{y}-xy)j \\  & =(x{e}^{y}-x)i-({e}^{y}-y)j \\ t(1,0) & =((1){e}^{0}-(1))i-({e}^{0}-(0))j \\  & =-j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $-j.$
